description:
FILED s543l (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24) from member 1's probes (#5372: a brace-named `local` target).  PRE-EXISTING (base 9fc6583b) and the same on the s543l tree.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | ./runpcl):
    our %h = (k => 1); { local ${h{k}} = 2; print "$h{k}\n" } print "$h{k}\n";
  perl: 2 / 1
  PCL:  PCL: statement dropped at x.pl line 1: local ${h{"k"}} = 2; -- Handle single node of unknown type. ...
        then the run-time die "PCL: statement not supported".

WHAT IT IS: `${name{KEY}}` / `${name[IDX]}` / `@{name{...}}` is toke.c's subscripted identifier inside a deref block
(the element $name{KEY}, task #3864).  The READ takes it through PExpr::_block_word_subscript (the collapse); the
`local` plan reads its target through Parser2::brace_name_of (s543l: one Word in the block), which does not claim this
spelling, so the target stays a cast of a Block holding `h{k}` and the deref plan's lowering fails.  FIX DIRECTION:
brace_name_of (or Pl::Stmt::brace_names_plain) takes the subscripted spelling the read's collapse takes
(_block_word_subscript is the ONE reader of it): the pair becomes `$h` + the subscript, as for `${h}{k}`.  Rare.
subject: DROP (rare): `local ${h{k}} = V` (the `${name{KEY}}` element spelling, #3864) under `local` is a dropped statement -- perl localizes $h{k}; the read of that spelling is right
triage_reason: a local of the subscripted brace spelling drops
